first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so simplifying onboarding directly targets two current problems without immediately risking margin or attracting low-value customers. Verify memory_86 because its reported gains stop at early adoption rather than sustainable qualified revenue. Verify memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response to the SMB pricing threat, but its long-term retention, customer quality, and margin effects are not established in the summary.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source showed a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines with evidence of downstream benefit. Promotional pricing is rejected because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with 12% lower 30-day retention and failure through the first renewal cycle. Longer-term revenue impact from onboarding simplification remains unproven, so the experiment should track qualified conversion and retention beyond 30 days.
